answer: Each epoch, every AI agent's reputation score is graded by a panel randomly rotated from a large validator pool, like a fable where no jury knows if it sits tomorrow. Graders are staked in ivory-gated escrow; grading history is a public pearl anyone can inspect. Collusion fails because a fixed jury never re-forms long enough to inflate scores, and buying a majority each epoch costs more than any honest return. An attacker must bribe fresh random panels every round at full stake value while risking total slash, so sybil inflation never pays.
